import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Reading the `bob ref` highlight-sync docs and code to see how Highlights annotations turn into ref notes. Reading the real sidecar and ref note for your Gas Town example, then the parser/renderer code. Checking how task dedup and block IDs would behave under a merge, then prior art (Readwise, Zotero, etc.). Code survey done (clean seam: only 3 consumers of parsed sidecar annotations). Now checking prior art — Readwise, Highlights, Zotero, MarginNote. Filed `bob-cli-9o` (block-ID churn bug) and added a +1 to `bob-cli-85` with the Gas Town text glitches. Reading the artifact policy, then writing the report. Writing the report now. Report written and registered. Submitting the final declaration. I recommend building this. Letting `bob ref` fold a highlight whose note starts with `<` into the one before it is the right gesture at the right layer, with five changes to the requirements described below. **Is it a good idea?** Yes. - **No PDF tool can do it.** PDF annotations always belong to a single page, and the Zotero and DEVONthink developers say the same. The fold has to happen in bob, which already rebuilds the ref note's highlights section from the Highlights sidecar on every scan. - **Readwise already does this.** You put `.c1` / `.c2` in the notes of the pieces, and they are joined with "…" when they sync to Readwise. Your `<` is simpler: one character, only on the second piece, because bob can rely on the sidecar's order. - **Your vault shows a real but small need.** About 4 of 338 annotations are page-split pairs. In one of them (`agent_catalog_pane`) you already wrote "…see above note" by hand. - **Guessing instead of a sigil would be wrong half the time.** A heuristic auto-merge on your vault was right only about 50% of the time. **Changes to your requirements:** 1. **When `<` counts:** only when it is followed by a space or the end of the note, on the note's first line. That way ``, `
`, `<-` and `<3` stay ordinary text. 2. **"Previous" means the previous text highlight** in Highlights' sidebar order. Page-1 marker notes, sticky notes and image selections are skipped. Several `<` pieces in a row join into one passage. 3. **How the pieces join:** without a gap only when the next piece picks up mid-sentence on the next page, with hyphenated words rejoined. Any other join shows ` … `, so a quote stitched from different points in a paragraph isn't presented as one real sentence. 4. **Block IDs and tasks:** - The merged block keeps the first piece's `^h-` ID. - A follower's old ID is dropped without a "Removed highlight" tombstone. - Tasks from a follower's note keep their `[h::]` ID tied to that piece, so adding or removing `<` never creates duplicate tasks. Their `🔖` link points at the merged block. 5. **Failures are visible:** a `<` with nothing to join stays in the note as-is and is counted in the scan report. If you still see a `<` in the ref note, it didn't merge. There are no new flags or config, and nothing writes to the PDF, the sidecar, or the plugins. Only one existing note in the vault would change: the Gas Town one. The scan at 06:45 already rendered pages 11 and 12 as separate blocks, so the first scan after this ships will join them into one quote under Page 11 with "PR Merge Master?!" as its comment. It will drop `^h-434a5e5a2bc4` without adding a tombstone. **Found along the way:** - **New bug `bob-cli-9o`:** adding a highlight above existing ones on a page gives every later highlight on that page a new ID and tombstones the old ones. The Gas Town note's git history shows it: one inserted caption on p. 9 caused 3 of that note's 5 tombstones, and it breaks task backlinks. - **Text damage `bob-cli-85`:** the "B eads" and "b d-4f43s" text in your example comes from Highlights' own text extraction of bob web-clip PDFs; `pdftotext` reads those pages cleanly. That bead already tracks this, so I added your Gas Town example as a +1. Three questions are open for you: whether you'd rather always join pieces without a gap (prettier, but sometimes misleading), whether to add a "force a gap" form later, and whether sticky notes starting with `<` should attach to the highlight above. The report also has the implementation sketch and test plan. The report is registered as `file:explicit:97c045892ffb257825b9b0b1` (label `research:202610/highlight_continuation_merge__cld.md`) and will be committed to the research repo when this turn ends.
